source.original_title: 05/05/2026 - Igor Reoutt & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/05/2026 - Igor Reoutt & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: England, recently returned after two years living between Mexico and Colombia; works on US hours

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Prospect saw the handover live — 'And I see Harry there. All right, we'll do it. Thanks, man. See ya. What's up, man? Was that Kim?' — and the rep confirmed 'It was.' The rep then read the setter's notes back verbatim.

prospect.name: Igor Reoutt
prospect.occupation: Electrical and audio-visual contractor — lighting control and high-end audio for luxury second homes. Recently restarted the business. Formerly a jiu-jitsu coach at a gym his wife owned.
prospect.family_status: Going through a divorce; supporting himself plus one other household. Has a daughter who was taken off gluten as a baby after failure to thrive. His wife previously owned the local jiu-jitsu gym and sold it.
prospect.training_background: Ex-athlete — motocross, grappling and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, plus a background in tennis — and a former BJJ coach for kids. Activity dropped away over roughly the last year; current exercise is a couple of miles walking at night and EDM dancing a couple of times a month, which he calls 'probably the most vigorous exercise that I get'. Attempts push-ups most days but describes it as not regimented. Owns a 30 lb and a 60 lb kettlebell and has done halos, goblet squats and bottoms-up holds. Was around 165 lb at his lightest, which he found too light.
prospect.medical: History of head injuries from motocross. Symptom-free for about twenty years, then recurrence roughly four years ago which he attributes to cervical loading in grappling — 'I think it was from rolling on my neck, doing some stuff'. Stopped motocross and largely stopped jiu-jitsu as a result. Treated by an acupuncturist who specialises in head injuries and considers himself resolved: 'I'm clear on all that fronts.' No physician clearance referenced. Also reports restricted shoulder range of motion from his tennis background and wants a stronger core so he does not get back issues. Gluten-free for almost 20 years, family-wide, following his daughter's diagnosis-adjacent response to elimination.

signals: Lost ground to a compound hard season — head injuries, the end of his coaching gym, a divorce and a business restart: 'last six years have been kind of, kind of crazy'
The rep named the emotional shape of it and the prospect confirmed: 'Fell out of love with it, but definitely want to get back in there'
Wants the former athletic self back rather than a new one — 'get your mojo back', 'I just want to get back to myself'
Explicitly rejects the optimizer frame: 'I don't want to be like that 55-year-old dude who's taking TRT, trying to wear stupid shirts... I just want to be where my body wants to be'
Carries the regret in the form of excuses he can hear himself making: 'I've just been so busy or the weather's or I got sick or something. It's just, it's always been something.'

goals.text: Get back into a routine and rebuild strength after roughly a year of near-inactivity
Lose 10 to 15 pounds and recompose — down from 180-185 toward 170-175 without getting ultra jacked
Build a good core so he does not get back issues, and good shoulders
Return to grappling and be strong enough not to be at a disadvantage on the mat
Get his mojo and body positivity back — 'I just want to get back to myself'
Functional strength that transfers to awkward, heavy tool work as an electrician
Learn the movements properly and be taught enough to run it himself afterwards

pains.text: Fell out of love with training after his coaching gym stopped being a happy place — 'it became a stressful place. So I just kind of backed out of it 100%'
Roughly a year of inactivity with a rotating set of reasons — 'I've just been so busy or the weather's or I got sick or something. It's just, it's always been something.'
Head injuries from motocross that recurred about four years ago and ended both motocross and most of his jiu-jitsu
Restricted shoulder range of motion from years of tennis
Financial instability during a divorce while supporting two households and restarting a business — 'some months are good... and some months you're like oh how am I gonna make all this work'
Training is not regimented — tries push-ups daily, nothing structured
Not in horrible shape but not in great shape either, and aware of the gap

objections.raw_quote: that I just gotta see if I can swing just because I am uh I'm going through a divorce and so like I'm supporting myself and then I've got something else that I'm supporting and you know it's um some months are good and it's not an issue uh and some months you're like oh how am I gonna make all this work
objections.rep_response: Asked a genuine diagnostic — 'Is it the like upfront amount that's concerning? It's like it's 6k upfront or what's the logistical concern for you?' — then, on hearing that both lump sum and monthly felt tough, invented a one-month entry at $1,200 and later offered a flexible two-payment structure of $3,000 down and $3,000 at two or three months.

objections.raw_quote: That's a, that's a commitment. Holy .
objections.rep_response: Held the frame briefly and well — 'Supposed to be brother, you know?' — then within thirty seconds pivoted to the business tax write-off pitch rather than to the value or the consequence of inaction.

objections.raw_quote: If it were 6k upfront, that would be tough to do. I mean, I was thinking more like it would probably be a monthly thing. Honestly, both just seem a little tough... I just need to see where things are going because I recently just restarted my business.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and reframed around cash timing — 'what I don't expect you to do is pull 6K out of your [pocket] if you don't have 6K to pull out' — then offered the one-month $1,200 entry as a way to buy himself time to gather cash.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, let me just, let me do a little forecasting and see where, where things are.
objections.rep_response: Accepted without a play, agreed a WhatsApp channel, confirmed his number and set the expectation for a morning answer so he could keep his phone off overnight.

tiers.note: Standard tier. Restated by both parties as 'a G a month'.

Improvised on the call in response to the affordability objection: 'you can start with one month, you get in there, you do your stuff with Trevor, you go for a month, it'll be 1200'. Not a standard tier.
Also quoted as an ongoing monthly rate — 'if you do it monthly it works out to be more, like it is 1200 a month' — which implies $7,200 over six months against the $6,000 headline.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three routes offered, all improvised in the last ten minutes: (1) two payments of $3,000 — '3K down, 3K in two months or something like that, or in three months. I don't mind making that flexible'; (2) a single month at $1,200 with the option at the end of the month to 'just pay the rest or we can set up a payment structure'; (3) rolling monthly at $1,200. Payment must precede the onboarding call — prospect asked 'I would assume we got to make the commitment and the payment before I talk to Trevor, right?' and the rep confirmed 'That's right, yeah.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Implied exit only, not a guarantee: 'if you hate it, you can obviously not continue on with it' after the first month.

evidence: No decision and no payment: 'let me do a little forecasting and see where things are. I'll get back to you'
Deferred deliberately to the next morning so the rep could sleep — 'Leave your phone off. Give me till the morning' — with WhatsApp agreed as the channel and numbers exchanged on the call
Real intent present: he wanted the onboarding call the next day ('Yeah, I'm trying to do it tomorrow') and engaged fully with the method

Counter-evidence: the blocker is genuine financial instability, not hesitation — a divorce, two households and a recently restarted business, with the prospect saying both the lump sum and the monthly 'seem a little tough'
Counter-evidence: no deposit was requested to hold anything, unlike two other follow-ups the same week
outcome.next_step: Prospect to forecast his cash position overnight and message on WhatsApp in the morning; if yes, onboarding call with Trevor the following day, payment first.

notable.note: Three things. First, the clinical one: the setter's notes flagged illness, the rep read it back, the prospect disclosed motocross head injuries that recurred four years ago from loading his neck in grappling, and the rep's entire response was 'I'm glad you're feeling good' — on a call that later described a first circuit of 'swings into snatches'. The only clearance referenced is an acupuncturist. Second, the price moved from $6,000 to an invented $1,200 one-month entry within four minutes of the affordability objection. Third, and most serious commercially, the tax pitch escalated from 'speak to your accountant' on earlier calls to an explicit offer to issue a framed invoice: 'We can create an invoice for you and frame it so you can write it off.' The rep also disclosed that only two closers exist and that he and the other one live together in Tulum.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion. The opening exchange has the prospect's label on the rep's questions and vice versa from 00:00:30 to 00:01:11. The rep's own scoliosis disclosure at 00:03:25 is correctly placed and matches his identical line on the Parker Stratton and Michael Angel calls. Long merged blocks at 00:10:02 to 00:11:22, 00:28:52 to 00:30:14 — which contains the entire tax-invoice passage split across both labels — and 00:35:52 to 00:38:22, where the rep's disclosure about living in Tulum with the other closer and the improvised payment structures run together as one unpunctuated stretch. Several profanities appear redacted. All roles read from content.
